name: More speciality medical education programmes to be offered in Dar

content.title: More speciality medical education programmes to be offered in Dar
content.summary: The University in partnership with the Aga Khan Hospital in Dar es Salaam is adding to its postgraduate medical education (PGME) programme in Tanzania to include surgery and internal medicine specialities.

media.alt: More speciality medical education programmes to be offered in Dar

content.text: The University in partnership with the Aga Khan Hospital in Dar es Salaam is adding to its postgraduate medical education (PGME) programme in Tanzania to include surgery and internal medicine specialities. Each of these four-year programmes, due to commence in January 2016, are in addition to the already existing programme in family medicine.

There is an acute need for physicians and health professionals in East Africa and even more so for medical specialists. This new development at the University promises increased availability of highly skilled doctors in the region and access to specialist care locally.

"The University is committed to increasing capacity and strengthening   healthcare systems by making high impact speciality medical education available in Tanzania and in the East Africa region," said Dr Nuruddin Lakhani, director, PGME.
The Tanzania Commission for Universities has approved both programmes; earlier this year, AKU received its charter as an international university in Tanzania.

The trainings are practice-based and residents will receive a stipend plus benefits. Additionally, the programmes are geared towards training graduates to take up leadership roles, in raising the quality of care and strengthening health systems in the region.
An open day at the end of August is being organised for interested candidates to meet with faculty and residents and view the facilities.
